$comment: AI ships at sea (PRD sections 4 and 6). About 'population' ships sail at once, by role share (the famous pirates, pirates.json, sail over and above it). A merchant buys at most voyageUnits a voyage, and only while the far port pays minMargin over its price; no more than maxPerRoute sail the same port pair at once. They skim a trade rather than flood it, so prices move without the player's routes drying up (checked by a route probe). Every ship is drawn by the 3D view, however far out it zooms; sightTiles (from the player's ship, times nightSight after dark) decides what the chart and minimap remember, and (at full range, day or night) which ship I intercepts, which AI fights play out on the map for her to join, and which gunfire she hears. Hailing works within hailTiles. Lanes are found on a grid of laneCell x laneCell tiles; each ship keeps her own line up to laneSpreadTiles to one side of a lane, so ships sharing it sail side by side; beating to windward, she tacks in boards up to tackTiles off it. Ships lie in port portDays before sailing on. Pirates mark ports near their haven (by size, interest halving at pirateRangeTiles) and lie in wait lurkDays on the lane. Convoys (PRD section 6, slice 2): each line sails on a timetable (every everyDays from firstDay): from the Atlantic entry off the map's east edge (or from a port, for the treasure ship) to one of its ports in turn, bringing goods and settlers (people: a share of the port's people), then loading what it takes and sailing home. Its coming is news. Merchants never call at the ports of a nation at war with theirs. A patrol at war sails to blockade an enemy port with chance blockade.chance, lying within blockade.tiles for blockade.days; otherwise patrols head for their ports where merchants have been lost in the last patrolLosses.days days. Each role draws her class from 'classes' by weight (her own stream, so the draw moves nothing else); the debug spawn sails the role's classId. A pirate sails biggerPirates.classId instead at odds rising to its maxShare as the player's strength (crew x (1 + guns/10)) grows from 'from' to 'full'. Convoys sail merchantmen, the Spanish flota a galleon, the treasure ship a treasure galleon. Danger (slice 2 of docs/design/combat-model.md): each sea area has a tier, 1 quiet (the Caribbean Sea, the Lesser Antilles) to 4 the treasure routes (the Gulf of Mexico); a pirate marks ports in waters that fit her ship's rung ('danger.classRung'), so sloops haunt the quiet coasts and brigantines the Main; the HUD names the waters' tier. Fits (slice 5): each AI ship carries the shipwright's upgrades by her role, each at its chance in 'fits' (navy planking and bronze, pirates copper and swivels, merchants nettings), so a well-fitted prize is worth more. Ships (slice 7): a role's 'byNation' adds classes to the mix for that nation's ships (Spain's guarda costa half-galleys, England's galley-frigate); pirates sail pinnaces and periaguas too, and merchants ketches and pinks.
